content.thinking:
The cursor encodes both sortValue and id, but the keyset predicate only uses sortValue and ignores the id.

Duplicate timestamps cause skipped or repeated rows. The user reports fewer results at the end, missing imported issues, a notification inbox count mismatch, and correct paging for gradually created entries.

The fix requires adding the id as a tiebreaker to the keyset predicate. For descending order, rows with the same sort value must be ordered by id. The sort direction still needs to be confirmed. A tenant scoping bug might also be causing entries from other workspaces to appear.

The bug is in `keysetPredicate`.

The predicate only checks `sortColumn < cursorSortValue`. When multiple rows share the same timestamp, the cursor's smaller id causes those entries to be skipped. This explains why identical-timestamp records disappear from pages.

The fix adds an `id < cursorId` tie-breaker when `sortColumn` equals the cursor value. This ensures identical-timestamp rows are not skipped. ISO string timestamps should sort correctly in SQL. The existing index can remain unchanged.

Checking existing tests for keyset pagination to confirm expected behavior. The predicate is combined with org filters via `and(...)`, so Drizzle should parenthesize the OR correctly and prevent tenant leaks.

Drizzle's `and()` does wrap OR conditions in parentheses. Without explicit parentheses, SQL operator precedence would place the OR before the AND, causing the org filter to be ignored on the second clause and leaking cross-tenant entries.
Checking Drizzle's OR/AND implementation.

content.thinking: Checking whether the and/or implementation wraps expressions in parentheses.

The fix is in keysetPredicate.

The cursor predicate for descending order must use strict less-than on the sort column, or equal sort plus strict less-than on the id column. ULIDs are time-ordered but not strictly monotonic within the same millisecond.

The ORDER BY clause is `desc(createdAt), desc(id)`. A cursor that only checks `createdAt` would skip every row sharing that timestamp. The predicate must also enforce `id` ordering to match the total sort order exactly.

The same keysetPredicate bug affects the issue list, notification inbox, and audit log. Fixing it once will resolve pagination for all three. Comment, member, project, and search repository lists also rely on this helper.

All seven callers use descending sort by createdAt and id. The shared keyset fix is safe for every list.

Cursor encoding safely handles `|` characters in sort values because ISO timestamps and ULIDs never contain them. SQLite string comparison on ISO-8601 timestamps matches the ORDER BY clause exactly, so the strict less-than predicate is semantically correct.

The generated SQL wraps the keyset predicate in parentheses. Tenant isolation filters remain properly grouped and cannot leak across tenants.

The `eq` and `lt` conditions bind cursor values safely through the column encoder. A tuple comparison like `(created_at, id) < (?, ?)` was considered as an alternative, but SQLite tuple comparisons only work cleanly for ascending order.

SQLite tuple comparison `(a, b) < (ca, cb)` is equivalent to the descending keyset predicate. It evaluates to `a < ca OR (a = ca AND b < cb)`, so a single row-value comparison could replace the current `or`/`and` logic.
The "Load more" UI component likely resides in the components directory.

The activity service's groupByDay function might be dropping items.

The missing entries are caused by a keyset tie-break bug, not day grouping. The fix belongs in `_paging.ts`. ULID columns should be compared as text. SQLite stores datetime as text.
The groupByDay sort has a bug when days are equal.

The pagination UI might not show a load-more option if nextCursor is missing.

The keyset pagination bug persists. I will fix `keysetPredicate` and update the Drizzle imports to include `and`, `eq`, `lt`, and `or`. I also need to check if `project-service` or `listIssuesWithRelations` drops items during page remapping, and whether a second offset-based path exists.

The keyset predicate must use a descending sort by timestamp and ID. The ID tie-break prevents skipping rows from bulk imports that share the same timestamp. SQLite NULL sort values are not a concern because createdAt is non-null. An edge case with equal sort values and ID comparisons also needs handling.

The `toOffset` function handles page-number pagination.

The issues page uses cursor pagination rather than page offset. The page number UI may be separate. Offset pagination without a stable sort would skip same-timestamp items.

OFFSET pagination would not permanently skip items. The symptom is a keyset cursor without a tiebreaker, which causes the header count to match but paging to return fewer unique items. I will fix the keyset predicate. I also need to check if any offset-based services re-slice results by createdAt.

The keyset predicate fix is complete. Comment and member repositories already order by createdAt and id, so cursors align with row IDs. SQLite text timestamps compare correctly with `<`. I am now writing the `keysetPredicate` implementation.

The `keysetPredicate` implementation now uses an `or()` clause. It compares the sort column first, then falls back to the ID column when timestamps match. This prevents bulk imports and audit rows from being dropped when they share a cursor timestamp.

The comment will stay concise. I will not add new tests or run extra scripts. The existing suite already covers this fix.

I am second-guessing whether to run a quick reproduction test. I will reason through the SQL generation instead. I need to confirm that Drizzle's SQLite dialect does not double-parenthesize the `or()` keyset predicate when it is spread into an existing `and()` filter.

Drizzle preserves parentheses from `or()` and `and()` when building the WHERE clause, so nesting is safe. SQLite binary collation handles ULID comparisons correctly because both sides are bound parameters. I should also check whether sort column values might have different precision.
